title: What Argentina Needs to Fulfill its AI Ambitions
gist: Soledad Guilera argues that Milei's UN pitch of tax breaks, limited AI-agent liability and no preemptive regulation will not make Argentina an AI hub, because its real bottlenecks are infrastructure (GPUs, data centers, transmission), shrinking talent pipelines and weak data-protection trust rules. She proposes a four-step plan: funded infrastructure, talent programs, a modern data law, and the state leading by example.

insights.claim: At the 2026 UN General Assembly, Argentine President Javier Milei invited global AI development in Argentina, offering tax breaks, limited liability for companies operating with AI agents, and a promise not to preemptively regulate AI.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Sets the policy baseline investors are being asked to price for Argentine AI/data center projects.
insights.locator: BUENOS AIRES—At last month’s UN General Assembly

insights.claim: Guilera argues that rules are not what is holding Argentina's AI sector back; its development hinges on building certainty for all parties rather than on deregulation.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Deregulation alone is unlikely to unlock AI FDI into Argentina; watch for certainty-building measures instead.
insights.quote: It’s clear that rules aren’t holding the country back.

insights.claim: The EU has had to delay parts of its AI Act because the technical standards needed for compliance were not ready, illustrating the cost of hasty rulemaking on immature technology.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Regulatory timelines for EU AI compliance remain fluid, affecting AI vendors' compliance costs.
insights.locator: The appeal is understandable.

insights.claim: For consumers and professionals such as doctors, loan officers and benefit recipients, the absence of AI rules is a source of risk rather than freedom, causing them to hold back from adoption when accountability is unclear.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Regulatory vacuums can suppress AI adoption and thus revenue for AI deployers in emerging markets.
insights.quote: For them, the absence of rules is a source of risk, rather than freedom.
insights.locator: Investors aren’t the only ones waiting

insights.claim: Guilera argues that clear accountability rules would strengthen rather than undermine Milei's proposal for companies run by AI agents, since such companies are easier to accept when everyone knows who answers for them.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Liability clarity is a precondition for commercial viability of agent-operated corporate structures.
insights.locator: None of this works against business.

insights.claim: Investors will not commit capital to Argentina's AI sector on a promise alone; they need credible signals of certainty.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Expect slow conversion of AI announcements into Argentine capex absent concrete legal and infrastructure steps.

insights.claim: Argentina's knowledge services industry generated a record $9.6 billion in export revenues last year.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Shows a sizeable existing tech-services export base that AI could build on.
insights.locator: Milei’s ambition is admirable

insights.claim: YPF, Argentina's state-controlled oil company, uses an AI agent in Vaca Muerta to flag operational problems before they happen.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Points to AI-driven efficiency in Argentine shale operations.
insights.locator: Milei’s ambition is admirable

insights.claim: Chile, Brazil and Uruguay lead the 2026 Latin American AI Index while Argentina ranks sixth of 20, and all three leaders score the same as Argentina on the regulation indicator, implying lack of AI legislation does not preclude success.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Regional AI leadership is driven by infrastructure and talent, not AI laws; Chile/Brazil/Uruguay are the relative winners.
insights.locator: In Latin America, even countries without

insights.claim: Brazil's Senate approved a comprehensive AI bill in 2024, but it has been stuck in the lower house since; Chile and Uruguay have no AI law either.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Regulatory overhang for AI in Brazil remains unresolved.
insights.locator: In Latin America, even countries without

insights.claim: Countries outranking Argentina on AI have focused on building data centers, training AI talent, sustaining research teams, driving corporate adoption, and using AI in government to engage citizens.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Provides a checklist for judging which LatAm markets will attract AI investment.
insights.locator: Although Argentina already has solid data

insights.claim: Argentina accounts for just 2.3% of Latin America's GPUs and 1.1% of its processing power, and has seven certified data centers versus Chile's 37.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Argentina is a very small compute market; Chile is the regional data center hub.
insights.locator: Argentina faces three key constraints

insights.claim: Argentina's last major high-voltage transmission line was completed in 2017, and the government's $6.6 billion catch-up transmission plan presented in May of last year is only now reaching the bidding stage.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Grid constraints limit data center buildout; transmission tenders are a pipeline opportunity for contractors.
insights.locator: Argentina faces three key constraints

insights.claim: Guilera recommends that every AI-related incentive in Argentina be paired with a funded plan for transmission lines and computing power, with guaranteed access for local researchers and companies.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Signals potential conditionality on AI incentives that could affect project economics.
insights.locator: Infrastructure improvements are the first key step.

insights.claim: Argentina's AI talent problem is no longer mainly brain drain but a shortage of professionals with the skills employers need.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Labor availability for AI operations in Argentina may be tighter than headline engineer counts suggest.
insights.locator: Talent supply is another gap.

insights.claim: Argentine federal science spending is on track to fall to about 0.16% of GDP this year from 0.30% in 2023, a real cut of more than 40%.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Austerity is hollowing out the public research base that supplies AI talent.
insights.locator: Talent supply is another gap.

insights.claim: Staff at Argentina's seven main federal science and technology agencies fell 13% from December 2023 to August 2026, which research group EPC attributes to cuts, closures, retirements, selective layoffs and restructuring.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Quantifies the human-capital cost of Milei's austerity on the innovation system.
insights.locator: Talent supply is another gap.

insights.claim: Guilera proposes government, universities and companies jointly fund AI retraining for data analysts and engineers, expand graduate training, share compute with researchers, and protect a stable core of AI research teams with multiyear funding that survives budget cycles.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Potential public-private partnership opportunities in AI education and compute.
insights.locator: Developing talent is the second step.

themes.theme: Trust deficit: data protection and cybersecurity

insights.claim: Argentina's data protection law dates from 2000, treats consent as the default basis for using personal data, regulates automated decisions only by courts and public agencies, and caps fines at 100,000 pesos (about $65).
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Legal ambiguity on training data use raises risk for AI firms operating in Argentina.
insights.locator: Trust is the third bottleneck.

insights.claim: The ITU Global Cybersecurity Index places Argentina in the fourth of its five tiers, and Argentina's data protection authority opened an investigation last December into a massive alleged leak of citizens' personal data.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Weak cyber posture is a risk factor for data center and cloud investment.
insights.locator: Trust is the third bottleneck.

insights.claim: Argentina's data protection authority drafted a modern data law in 2023 with legal grounds beyond consent, human review of automated decisions, high-risk impact assessments and cloud transfer safeguards, but the bill lapsed in Congress despite Argentina ratifying a Council of Europe convention committing it to these standards.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: A ready-made bill exists; its revival would be a fast, cheap catalyst for AI investment certainty.
insights.locator: The third step is to update

insights.claim: Reviving Argentina's lapsed 2023 data protection bill would be a low-cost, high-value signal to investors and citizens.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Watch for this bill as a leading indicator of AI-policy seriousness.
insights.quote: Reviving it would be a low-cost, high-value signal.
insights.locator: The third step is to update

insights.claim: Guilera urges the Argentine state to lead by example: showcase its AI assistant in an official app reaching 26 million people, publish a list of algorithms the state uses including in security and defense, and impose cybersecurity standards and breach-reporting duties on public agencies.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Public-sector AI and cybersecurity procurement could grow if adopted.

insights.claim: Two weeks before Argentina's October 2025 midterms, the government announced a Patagonia data center worth up to $25 billion based on a letter of intent between OpenAI and a local energy company, but a year later it does not appear among projects approved under the incentive regime it was meant to use.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Headline AI megaproject announcements in Argentina should be heavily discounted until approvals materialize.

insights.claim: A new Argentine incentive law for AI and data centers, approved by the lower house in June, still awaits a Senate vote, and a bill allowing companies to operate through AI agents has sat in a Senate committee since June without a formal report.
insights.speaker: SOLEDAD GUILERA
insights.so_what: Legislative catalysts for Argentine data center investment remain pending.
